_about: Packages the installers add to `pip install -e .[all,dev]` on each platform, because pyproject.toml cannot
carry them: forks installed from a git tag or a GitHub release (docs/PLATFORMS.md section 4) and platform
pins. scripts/install_windows.ps1, install_macos.sh and install_linux.sh read this file, and so does
`quantabench-cli update` (Help > Check for updates...): after a pull that changes an entry it reinstalls that
package, and --upgrade-packages keeps all of them. packages: requirement strings. only_binary: names passed as
--only-binary (never build from source). find_links: package name -> URL passed as --find-links; point it at
a new release and Update reinstalls that package, even when the version number stays the same.
Keep this file ASCII: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads it as ANSI.

windows._why: FORK-1: dxtb ported to tad-libcint 0.4 (GFN2, polarizability, IR intensities). FORK-2: tblite wheels (PyPI has none for Windows).

macos._why: FORK-1: PyPI's dxtb cannot use tad-libcint on macOS. tblite: never build from source (its newest wheels need macOS 15).

crest._why: FORK-5: conda-forge's osx-arm64 crest 3.0.2 links Apple's Accelerate and fails every optimization of 19+ atoms (docs/ENGINES.md). This is the fork's macOS build (brandonbtm29/crest, branch qb/macos, workflow qb-macos). install_macos.sh --with-engines downloads url, checks sha256, unpacks it under ~/Library/Application Support/QuantaBench/programs and sets exe as this machine's CREST path.
crest.built_by: brandonbtm29/crest Actions run 42295799792 (qb-macos, fork commit 12eb61d), artifact crest-macos-arm64; release that tarball unchanged, or put the new one's sha256 here
crest.until_released: Until then the conda crest of qb-tools is used, which fails on molecules of 19+ atoms: QuantaBench flags each one (conformer_fallback) and counts them at the end of a batch.

linux._why: GFN2-xTB in PyPI's dxtb needs tad-libcint below 0.4 (0.4 needs the dxtb fork; docs/INSTALL.md).
